text:
sara: FYI — during long-context canaries we've been seeing steady memory creep in the KV cache (up to +18% over 12h) and fragmentation ratio ~1.7. attaching profiler dump in thread.

mike: can you paste the profiler snippet? which canary is this?

sara: canary: longctx-chat-redispatch-2 (started ~3866920000). key metrics i pulled: 
```
heap_total: 24.2GB -> 28.6GB (12h)
kv_cache_slots: 3.2M
allocated_blocks: 1.12M
avg_block_size: 24.3B
fragmentation_ratio: 1.72
eviction_rate: 0.9/s -> 2.1/s
pager_spill_to_nvme: 0.7% of requests
```
Also the allocator free-list shows many small holes (8-64B) concentrated in the 32/64 bucket ranges. Pattern: repeated extending sequences -> allocate small tails -> later long-context pages create misses and allocate new small blocks instead of reusing holes.

leo: sounds like classic internal fragmentation caused by bucket granularity + allocation spread. if typical allocation ~24B and our buckets are 32/64, that's a lot of internal waste.

anya: paging + hole accumulation would explain the nvme spills. when a seq grows we don't fit into narrow holes and fall back to new allocations, pushing pressure that triggers paging.

taylor: have we tried compact-on-alloc? last time that spiked tail latencies because it runs in hot path.

mike: agree, avoid synchronous compaction in hot paths. proposal: background sliding-window compactor that consolidates contiguous holes when free fraction in a region exceeds a threshold. keep it low-priority and rate-limited.

sara: sketched prototype config:
```
kv.compaction.window_ms = 60000  # run interval for background sweeps
kv.compaction.region_size = 256KB
kv.compaction.free_threshold = 0.35  # trigger when >35% free in region
kv.allocator.small_buckets = [16,32,48,64]  # add non-power-of-two slot to reduce waste
kv.allocator.enable_spread = true  # try scatter allocations to reduce long-run holes
kv.sampler.prob = 0.02  # sample 2% of allocations to attempt in-place coalesce/hint
```
Idea: sampler tries a local quick coalesce / bucket remap for a small percent of allocations to detect heavy-hole regions cheaply. background compactor consolidates only cold regions and yields if scheduling latency rises.

leo: +1 for sampler and non-pow2 buckets. the 48B slot trades less internal waste for a slightly more complicated allocator. worth benchmarking.

anya: quick cpu estimate: on a host with 8 cores, background compactor that touches 256KB regions and runs ~once/min uses ~2-3% CPU when active in our synthetic traces. memory savings in test runs was 5-8% and nvme spills dropped by ~60%.

taylor: we need metrics to guard and observe: compaction.cycles, compaction.cpu_seconds, allocator.waste_bytes, allocator.hole_count_by_bucket, eviction.rate, eviction.p99_latency. rollout plan: A/B 10% traffic for 24h on long-context canaries.

mike: one caution: we saw a regression in a prior canary where compaction correlated with p99 token latency +40ms. we must add a backoff: if scheduler latency > 2x baseline or compaction.cpu_seconds per minute > X, pause compactor.

deploy-bot: canary deploy longctx-kv-compact-v1 started by mike at 3867008015

sara: next steps — i'll push sampler + non-pow2 bucket prototype to experimental branch, add the metrics/timers and the compactor backoff guard. mike will wire the canary A/B and dashboards. we'll reconvene tomorrow after the 24h run and decide whether to widen rollout.

mike: sounds good. i'll add the dashboard panels and a small alert for eviction.p99 > baseline + 20ms or OOMs. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
